# hg bundle

**What this page tells you:** every `hg bundle` subcommand, with its arguments, flags and defaults.

Front door: scaffold a new agent team repo.

## Synopsis

```text
hg bundle init <dir> [flags]
```

`--json` prints one JSON document on stdout; narration goes to stderr.

## Description

The agent-bundle loop's entry. `init` scaffolds an agent-team repo in the `harness-hg/` tree - the team's `harness-hg/{team,destination,workspaces}.yaml` and one Eve agent per `--agents` entry under `agents/eve/<name>/{harness-hg,src}` (Hermes is frozen legacy and is refused with the copy-from-examples path) - writes only what it can fill honestly (an absent `harness-hg/*.yaml` is a feature that is off, listed in the README), proves the scaffold passes `hg validate --dir` on its own output, and prints the loop. Unrelated to profile bundles (harness-hg/bundles.yaml - many profiles, one pod).

## `hg bundle init`

```text
hg bundle init <dir> [flags]
```

Scaffold a new agent-bundle repo and prove it validates.

| Flag | Value | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--agents` | `<list>` | — | The agents to scaffold, `<harness>:<name>` comma-separated (`eve:manager,eve:research`; a bare name is Eve). Hermes is refused. |
| `--agent` | `<name>` | — | One Eve agent by name (DNS-1123, ≤40; default: the team name, the directory basename minus `.harness-hg`). Alternative to --agents. |
| `--gitops` | `<url>` | — | The GitOps destination repo written into harness-hg/destination.yaml. |
| `--dry-run` | — | — | Print the steps; write nothing. |

**Examples**

```bash
hg bundle init ../my-team --agents eve:manager,eve:research --gitops https://github.com/org/my-team.gitops.git
hg bundle init ../solo --agent solo
```
